Question: Have you ever tried pairing nuts with meat (chicken, beef, or fish)? What is your experience, and what do you recommend?
Answer: Nuts and Meat go great together The first thing that came to mind was Peanuts. Thai cuisine has a wonderful peanut sauce and the West Africans make a great chicken peanut stew. Alas peanuts are legumes and not nuts so I will have to disqualify them. The Chinese cuisine you find in the United States often pairs nuts & meat together. They stir fry almonds or cashews with chicken in a savory-sweet sauce. It’s quite delicious. I love putting slivered almonds into my chicken salad. It adds a nice crunch and the creamy almonds blend with the mayonnaise in a wonderful way. You can also crush nuts up and use them to coat meat & fish. I love dishes like pecan coated chicken or almond crusted trout Nuts and meat can really work well together.

Question: How did you overcome the hardest times of your life?
Answer: By keeping a simple phrase in mind: “This too shall pass.” I learned this phrase reading a fable. “In the fable of a powerful king (I recall it being King Solomon) asks his assembled wise men to create a ring that will make him happy when he is sad. After deliberation the sages hand him a simple ring with the words "This too will pass" etched on it, which has the desired effect to make him happy when he is sad. It also, however, became a curse for whenever he is happy.” It’s a really simple phrase but my mind can never let go of it and it really puts life in perspective for me. Whatever seems like your darkest moment now, a year, 5 years, 10 years from now it may hardly be remembered. It also keeps me humble when things are going well. Was very life changing for me once I adopted it as a core philosophy.

Question: How do you know the Pantone color from CMYK?
Answer: I’m not sure what you are asking exactly but if you are wondering how you can tell if pantone or cmyk inks were used in a printed item you can tell by looking at the image with a magnifying glass. When you zoom in on a printed image you will start to see a little dot pattern from the four different cmyk inks being layers to create the full color spectrum. Pantone inks are just whatever shade you ordered already pre mixed in the can. There is no dot pattern other than a halftone screen used if you want a tint of the solid color to print.
